subject: Unified rollback decision & customer briefing for p95 spike
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T08:12:05-07:00
Subject: Unusual p95 spike & throughput drop - investigating

Team,

Alerting: between 07:48-08:05 PT we observed a coordinated p95 latency spike (from ~420ms -> 1.9s) and a concurrent throughput drop (~22% of expected tokens/sec) affecting the gen-api route for customers using model-v3-quant. The impact surface appears limited to requests with long context windows (>1k tokens) and KV cache miss patterns.

What we have so far:
- Initial root indicators: sudden kernel-scheduling stalls on a subset of pods (see attached incident_trace.log).
- Not all racks affected; traffic skewed to a small set of GPU pools serving model-v3-quant.
- Automatic fallback to model-v3-fp32 triggered for some requests but not consistently due to policy mismatch.

Immediate asks:
1) Product: do we want an immediate config rollback to model-v3-quant@rev-202803 (safer) or enable the broader model fallback policy (allowing v3-fp32) as primary mitigation? Both have cost/quality tradeoffs.
2) CS (Grace): flag impacted OlivePay customers and prep a brief customer-facing note.
3) Eng (Ben/Markus): patch or OOS change ETA? If we plan a rollback, we need a canary window and orchestration steps.

I've attached the trace and a short log slice. I'm spinning up an isolated pool to drain affected racks and will post an update in 20m.

- Dylan

[Attachment: incident_trace.log (text)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T09:05:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual p95 spike & throughput drop - investigating

Thanks for the quick signal, Dylan.

High level guidance from product: our priority is minimizing customer impact while avoiding regressions in quality. Quick notes:
- For OlivePay (large real-time payments workload), a temporary quality drop (fp32 fallback) is acceptable if it restores latency and throughput within the SLA window.
- Prefer automated fallback rather than a full rollback if it can be enacted in the next 15-30 minutes. Rollback is heavier and risks version skew for other tenants.

Concrete asks:
1) Eng: can you confirm whether enabling the broader fallback policy will immediately route impacted requests to v3-fp32 for OlivePay only (route-based override)? If yes, please do that as mitigation and share the exact change and timing so CS can notify customers.
2) If fallback is not fast enough, prepare a rollback play (rev-202803) with a 5% canary window, 10-minute observation, then progressive ramp.
3) Operations: capture a temp SLA exception if we expect >5% request errors for >30 minutes; we can negotiate credits later.

Grace, draft a 1-2 line note for OlivePay saying we're aware, mitigation underway, ETA tentative 30-45m. I'll review.

Soojin: can you coordinate the external comms approval thread? I'll escalate to leadership if this grows beyond an hour.

- Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Serving
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual p95 spike & throughput drop - investigating

On Wed, May 3, 2028 at 09:05, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Concrete asks:
> 1) Eng: can you confirm whether enabling the broader fallback policy will immediately route impacted requests to v3-fp32 for OlivePay only (route-based override)? If yes, please do that as mitigation and share the exact change and timing so CS can notify customers.

Quick update and recommendation:
- Root cause: a kernel scheduling regression in the CUDA runtime we pulled in via kernel-optimizer@1.14; manifests as latency amplification when KV cache misses align with long context. The regression is isolated to the quantized execution path (model-v3-quant).
- Mitigation options evaluated:
  A) Enable route-overrides to prefer model-v3-fp32 for OlivePay traffic: LOW risk, immediate, increases cost ~30-40% for those requests, quality diff minimal for short prompts.
  B) Rollback model-v3-quant to rev-202803: MEDIUM risk operationally (canary required), likely restores perf everywhere but takes ~25min to execute safely.
  C) Hotfix patch to kernel-optimizer: HIGH confidence fix but requires building and pushing a new runtime and is ~90-120min.

Recommendation: choose A now to stabilize customer experience, start B in parallel as a rollback safety if A doesn't fully restore throughput after 15 minutes. I'll enact A now for OlivePay and post the change-id. If A doesn't reach acceptable p95 in 15m we'll trigger B canary.

Planned change: route-override (service: gen-api, route: olivepay-prod) -> prefer model-v3-fp32. Change id: CHG-20280503-01. Rolling to 2 canaries immediately and then to 10% traffic for 5m.

Attachments: small diff to automate rollback in case we need it (hotfix_patch.diff).

- Ben

[Attachment: hotfix_patch.diff (text)]

From: Zachary Liu <zach@olivepay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops <ops@olivepay.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual p95 spike & throughput drop - investigating

Thanks for the quick response and the plan.

We're seeing elevated latencies on our side and it's affecting settlement windows. Enabling the fallback to fp32 is acceptable as a short-term mitigation. Can you confirm:
- ETA for the fallback taking full effect for our production traffic?
- If the 15-minute check shows incomplete recovery, please let us know before you run the rollback so we can coordinate traffic shifting on our end.

Also, please keep us updated if you expect any request-level differences we should be aware of (e.g., small semantic drift for long-context prompts).

Appreciate the transparent cadence.

—Zach
Support Lead, OlivePay
